issues.title: Logging middleware shares mutable state across requests
issues.detail: A single `LoggingMiddleware` instance is created and shared across all routes. Its `startTime` field is written in `OnRequest` and read in `OnResponse`, so concurrent requests overwrite each other's start time, producing incorrect durations and a data race.

issues.title: Default CORS allows credentials with wildcard origin
issues.detail: CORS defaults to enabled with origins `*` and `allowCredentials: true`. When credentials are on, `getAllowOrigin` still returns `"*"` via the loop fallback. Browsers reject `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` when `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`.

issues.title: Logging middleware race on startTime
issues.detail: One `LoggingMiddleware` instance is shared across all concurrent requests. `OnRequest` writes `m.startTime` and `OnResponse` reads it, so overlapping requests corrupt each other's timing.

issues.title: CORS wildcard with credentials
issues.detail: Defaults set `allowedOrigins=["*"]` and `allowCredentials=true`. Line 65 guards the simple case, but the loop at line 76 still returns `"*"` when credentials are on, causing both `*` and `Allow-Credentials: true` headers to be sent—which browsers reject per the Fetch spec.

children.unsure: The claim that browsers reject `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with `Allow-Credentials: true` is a Fetch spec rule not provable from the repository alone.

AUTHORED.title: Logging In
AUTHORED.sub: Authenticate via credentials or SSO proxy, issue and validate JWT tokens, and manage session state across legacy and v2 frontends.

group.note: Auth domain, middleware, API handler, and frontend are peers, not sequential.

AUTHORED.detail: Users submit credentials to `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, which returns a signed HS256 JWT. Every subsequent request passes through `AuthMiddleware` (and optionally `AuthSSOProxyMiddleware`) that validates the token and sets the account in the request context.

issues.title: Secret key regenerated on every restart by default
issues.detail: When `SHIORI_HTTP_SECRET_KEY` is not set, a random UUID is used. Every restart invalidates all existing JWTs, logging out every user. The warning is logged but easy to miss in containers.

children.title: Auth Domain Logic
children.sub: Credential verification with timing-attack protection, JWT creation and validation
children.detail: `AuthDomain` checks passwords with bcrypt, signs JWTs with HS256, and validates tokens by parsing claims then re-fetching the account from the database to get current config.

rows.title: Look up username
rows.detail: Queries `ListAccounts` with `WithPassword: true`. If no match, bcrypt-compares against a dummy hash so the response time is equal.

rows.title: Compare password
rows.detail: `bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword` on the stored hash. Returns `ErrInvalidCredentials` on mismatch.

rows.title: Create JWT
rows.detail: Embeds the `AccountDTO` in a custom claim, sets `ExpiresAt`, and signs with `jwt.SigningMethodHS256` using `Config().Http.SecretKey`.

rows.title: Validate on later requests
rows.detail: `CheckToken` parses the JWT, validates the HMAC signature, then re-reads the account from the DB by ID so config changes take effect.

issues.title: No token revocation on logout
issues.detail: HandleLogout clears the `token` cookie but the JWT itself remains valid until it expires. A captured token can be replayed for up to 30 days.

issues.title: Refresh always grants 30-day expiration
issues.detail: HandleRefreshToken unconditionally sets 30 days regardless of whether the original login used RememberMe. A 1-hour session can be extended to 30 days by calling refresh.

issues.title: dbbase.withTx swallows commit failures
issues.detail: The Commit call is in a deferred closure that logs but does not return the error. On the success path the caller receives nil even if the commit fails, risking silent data loss. On the error path the deferred Commit runs after Rollback, logging a confusing extra error. This affects MySQL and PostgreSQL; SQLite overrides withTx with a correct implementation.

issues.title: DeleteBookmarks with no IDs deletes everything
issues.detail: All three backends treat an empty ID list as 'delete all': they execute unconditional DELETE FROM bookmark_tag and DELETE FROM bookmark. The variadic signature makes calling with no arguments easy to do by accident, silently nuking all data.

issues.title: SetDatabaseSchemaVersion leaks a transaction
issues.detail: The method calls MustBegin() opening transaction 1, then calls withTx() opening transaction 2. Transaction 1 is never used and just leaks until the deferred Rollback fires. Inside withTx the callback explicitly calls Commit(), and then the deferred Commit in withTx runs again. Compare with MySQL's correct single-transaction version.

children.title: Schema Migrations
children.sub: Embedded SQL files and a semver-based runner that upgrades each backend's schema
children.detail: Migration SQL is embedded via `//go:embed` and `runMigrations` walks a version chain, executing each step matching the current schema version. Each backend defines its own ordered migration list.

code.label: runMigrations: walk list, match version, execute, update
newFileMigration: reads embedded SQL and runs in transaction

rows.title: Read current version
rows.detail: Calls GetDatabaseSchemaVersion to fetch the semver string from shiori_system.

rows.title: Match migration
rows.detail: Walks the migration list looking for one whose fromVersion equals the current version.

rows.title: Execute migration
rows.detail: Runs the migration function (SQL file in a transaction, or a custom Go function) on the writer DB.

rows.title: Update version
rows.detail: Calls SetDatabaseSchemaVersion with the toVersion, then loops back to step 2.
